source.text: A lumped body following a ramp in the coolant temperature: C dT/dt = -h A (T - T_b(t)) with T_b linear; the answer lags the ramp by the time constant C / (h A) times its slope, and RK4 reproduces it. Heat capacity per metre 206.404 J/m/K, outer surface 29.8451 mm2/mm. The pin warms monotonically, so the largest peak is the value at 40 s: 802.017 K from 600 K. The tolerance is 1 % of the rise, fixed before any run (first-order step error 0.4 % at most, the lumped approximation, the 0.05 s the solver applies the new film value late).
source.check: Second method: FEED's independent finite-volume solution of the full pin with the history (src/core/transientFv.ts, tests/transientFvBoundary.test.ts, exact lumped solutions) and the real solver through tests/seedOracleBoundaryHistory.test.ts; the history is written to OFFBEAT as timeDependentAxialProfileHTC and judged by FEED's own cross-check in docs/boundary-history.md.

coverage.domain: synthetic pin with a conductivity of 400 W/m/K and a heat capacity of 3 MJ/m3/K (Biot about 0.005), no power, uniform 600 K start, film coefficient 500 W/m2/K, coolant ramping linearly from 600 to 900 K over 40 s
